title: Alterations in the Immune-Fibrotic Axis Are Spatially Localized in the Aging Heart

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Alterations in the Immune-Fibrotic Axis Are Spatially Localized in the Aging Heart》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · acel70768-sec-0001-p1】Aging poses one of the major risk factors for cardiovascular disease. In the mammalian heart, a persistent inflammatory state known as inflammaging is promoted by various repeated antigenic stimuli throughout life, driving the release of chronic low‐grade inflammatory signals (Ferrucci and Fabbri 2018). Cardiovascular inflammaging is associated with fibrosis, vascular dysfunction and impaired tissue homeostasis that together promote adverse cardiac remodeling, atherosclerosis, and heart failure (Chirinos et al. 2019; Liberale et al. 2025). Age‐related changes in cardiomyocyte function (Yucel et al. 2026) and the perivascular environment (Rodriguez Morales et al. 2025) include the accumulation of cells with senescence‐associated features defined by a set of hallmarks that includes cell‐cycle arrest (Abdellatif et al. 2023; Gorgoulis et al. 2019; SenNet Consortium 2022).

【Introduction · acel70768-sec-0001-p2】Cardiovascular inflammaging is driven primarily by a shift in immune and resident stromal cell interactions. In the adult heart, resident macrophages contribute to maintaining homeostasis by clearing pathogens and debris and influence fibrosis by interacting with other cells through antigen presentation, cytokine and chemokine signaling (Nicolas‐Avila et al. 2022). With advanced age, self‐sustaining protective resident macrophages are replaced by aggressive bone marrow‐derived macrophages that stoke chronic tissue inflammation. Adult cardiac fibroblasts retain an organ‐specific embryonic transcriptome (Forte et al. 2022; Furtado et al. 2016) and are normally responsible for routine extracellular matrix (ECM) maintenance by responding to biochemical and mechanical signals within the myocardium (Pesce et al. 2023; Tallquist and Molkentin 2017). In aged hearts, cardiac fibroblasts are induced by pro‐inflammatory macrophages to become chronically overactive, secreting cytokines and matrix‐remodeling proteins and driving localized fibrosis that recruits more immune cells, which accelerates tissue stiffening and functional decline (Frangogiannis 2019).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Alterations in the Immune-Fibrotic Axis Are Spatially Localized in the Aging Heart》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Bulk RNA‐Seq Data Processing and Analysis · acel70768-sec-0005-p1】Samples were processed using an internal RNA‐seq pipeline (https://github.com/TheJacksonLaboratory/cs‐nf‐pipelines/wiki/RNA‐Pipeline‐ReadMe) with default parameters. Raw reads were quality‐filtered and adapter‐trimmed using fastp (v0.23.2) and aligned to GRCm38 (Ensembl, v102) using RSEM (v1.3.1) with bowtie2 (v2.4.5). Alignment estimation of gene expression was performed using the Expectation–Maximization algorithm paired‐end read data. RSEM also generated gene‐level and isoform‐level expression estimates, producing gene counts, isoform counts, and BAM files for both genome‐aligned and isoform‐aligned reads. Post‐alignment quality control (QC) was conducted with FastQC (v0.11.9) and Picard CollectRnaSeqMetrics, and compiled using MultiQC. Normalization (trimmed Mean of M‐values) and differential expression analyses were done using the edgeR (v4.6.0), retaining genes with CPM > 1 in ≥ 2 samples and a generalized linear model (quasi‐likelihood F‐test, using sex, age, and their interaction term, FDR < 0.05) (Table S1). Sex was not a major overall driver specifically in the analysis of bulk RNA‐seqdata: 12 DEGs passed FDR < 0.05 with 7 of them on sex‐specific chromosomes (Table S2). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were analyzed using KEGG pathway (Kanehisa et al. 2025) with clusterProfiler (v4.16.0) in R and Gene Ontology (GO) terms (Gene Ontology Consortium et al. 2023) (Table S3).

【Visium Spatial Transcriptomics Library Preparation, Sequencing, Data Pre‐Processing, and Alignment · acel70768-sec-0012-p1】Each slide containing FFPE section (5 μm, ColorFrost Plus slides by Fisher) with the region of interest (ROI, 6.5 mm × 6.5 mm) was deparaffinized and hybridized with manufacturer‐provided mouse‐specific probe sets for mRNA labeling and transferred using the CytAssist (10× Genomics) onto a Visium CytAssist Slide; libraries were prepared per 10× Genomics Protocol CG000495, quantified using a Tapestation High Sensitivity DNA ScreenTape (Agilent) and fluorometry (Thermofisher Qubit), and verified via KAPA qPCR. The library final yield and concentrations ranges were 90–275 ng and 2.85–7.55 ng/μL, respectively. Pooled libraries were sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq X+ 10B 100 cycle flow cell (28‐10‐10‐90 read configuration), targeting 100,000 read pairs/spot. Illumina BCL files for all libraries were converted to FASTQs (bcl2fastq v2.20.0.422, Illumina). Slides were H&E stained (The JAX Histology Core; details online https://doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6qpvr3653vmk/v1), scanned (40X, Nanozoomer, HT2.0, Hamamatsu), and analyzed by NDP software. For each tissue section and corresponding library, the whole slide brightfield and CytAssist images were aligned manually using the Loupe Browser (v6.4.1) via landmark registration. Each whole slide image was uploaded to a local OMERO server where a rectangular ROI containing just tissue was drawn via OMERO.web. OMETIFF images of each ROI were programmatically generated using the OMERO Python API. FASTQ files, the image registration JSON file, and associated OMETIFF corresponding to high‐resolution brightfield image were further processed, including alignment to the pre‐built mouse transcriptome reference m10‐2020‐A‐specific filtered probeset (v1.0.0) using Space Ranger count pipeline (v2.1.0). Following alignment with Space Ranger, the number of spots under tissue ranged from 2373 to 3973 across the samples. Sequencing depth yielded with a cohort‐wide average of 5452.75 ± 2157.41 median genes per spot and of 33,079.00 ± 24,316.42 median UMI counts per spot.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Alterations in the Immune-Fibrotic Axis Are Spatially Localized in the Aging Heart》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Introduction · acel70768-sec-0001-p4】Single‐cell and spatial transcriptomic mouse heart atlases have already documented age‐related transcriptional changes in multiple cell types (Morsy et al. 2026; Schaum et al. 2020; Tabula Muris Consortium 2020; Tabula Muris Consortium et al. 2018; Vidal et al. 2019). Large‐vessel and perivascular niches in the aging left ventricle were specifically identified as prominent sites of inflammatory, fibrotic, and senescence‐associated changes (Rodriguez Morales et al. 2025). To extend these observations, we monitored the aging response of the entire heart using bulk RNA‐seq and characterized macrophages and fibroblast‐lineage cells using single nucleus RNA‐seq and spatial transcriptomics in 6‐ and 24‐month‐old C57BL/6J male and female mouse hearts (Figure S1). Spatial transcriptomic analysis of longitudinal cardiac sections encompasses all four chambers, valves, and proximal great vessels. Our findings shift the focus from distributed sites of aging throughout the myocardium toward sites of cardiac connective tissue and large‐vessel compartments, implicating valves and aorta as niches where the strongest inflammaging‐related changes are localized. Interestingly, resulting senescence‐associated transcriptional signatures from young and aged fibroblasts partially shared features also found in the human heart.

【FFPE Block DV200 Evaluation · acel70768-sec-0011-p1】FFPE cardiac sections were cut in the long‐axis (longitudinal) plane. Two to four 5 μm FFPE sections were obtained in RNAse‐free conditions. RNA was extracted using Qiagen's RNeasy Micro Kit (Cat. No./ID: 74004) and quantified using a Tapestation High Sensitivity RNA ScreenTape (Agilent). DV200 scores (% RNA sample > 200 bases in length, Agilent TapeStation Analysis software) > 50% was achieved for all sections.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Alterations in the Immune-Fibrotic Axis Are Spatially Localized in the Aging Heart》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · acel70768-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Age induces cardiac inflammation and remodeling changes and increases number of macrophages and Postn + fibroblasts. (A) Enriched KEGG pathways based on significant bulk RNA‐seq DEGs between young (6 m) and aged (24 m) mice (males and females combined; n = 3 per sex/age); FDR < 0.05; color scale (blue to red)—adjusted p value. (B) Significant age‐related module from weighted gene co‐expression network analysis (WGCNA); FDR < 0.05 (n = 3 per sex/age). (C) Expression heatmap of genes in the module from (B); color scale (green‐black‐red)—gene expression (lcpm‐log of counts per million). (D) Enriched GO BP (FDR < 0.05) based on genes in the age‐related WGCNA module. (E) Cardiac nuclei segregated according to cell types on the uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) embedding plot; combined young (6 m) and aged (24 m) males and females (n = 3 per sex/age); each point is a single nucleus, color represents cell type, Wilcoxon rank‐sum test. (F) Age‐related changes in cell composition: Nuclei count ratios (log2 ratio, aged/young) for each cell type in males and females; two‐proportion Z‐test (*p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001).

【FIGURE 2 · acel70768-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Aorta and valve areas had the highest estimated proportion of macrophages and Gsn + fibroblasts. Spot deconvolution of macrophages (A) and Gsn + fibroblasts (B) using snRNA‐seq transcriptional profiles as a reference to infer cell proportions (blue to red color scale—estimated proportions) as well as spatial expression of cell markers (C1qa—macrophages (A); Gsn—Gsn + fibroblasts (B)), Ccl8 (A) and Cdkn1a (B) using spatial transcriptomics data (Visium, 10× Genomics) (blue to red color scale—gene expression); representative examples, n = 3 sex/age.

【FIGURE 3 · acel70768-fig-0003】FIGURE 3 Aging macrophages and Gsn + fibroblasts acquire stromal‐associated and ECM remodeling transcriptional changes, respectively. Dot plots show top ten enriched GO BP (adj. p‐value < 0.05) based on significantly upregulated DEGs with aging (young vs. aged, n = 3 per age/sex, adj. p‐value < 0.05, log2FC > 0.36) in both sexes (A), males only (B), and females only (C). Dot color indicates the adjusted p‐value (red = more significant); dot size reflects the gene ratio (proportion of upregulated DEGs annotated to that term), per the scales shown below each panel with males and females only on the same scale.
